text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Disappointing results force KLM Royal Dutch Airlines to undergo thorough restructuring. (p1)
- Rabobank mulls alliance with pension fund PFV Pensioenen. (p1)
- Window blinds maker Hunter Douglas posts 8.9 pct rise in Q3 turnover, maintains optimistic full-year forecast. (p3)
- Stakeholders in Australian express delivery service TNT frustrate Dutch PTT's (KPN) takeover plans. (p3)
- Royal Dutch/Shell is considering stopping PVC production. (p3)
- Chip machinery manufacturer Besi Q3 net profit drops to 6.7 million guilders from 11.4 million in Q2. (p4) DE VOLKSKRANT
- Netherlands on course to meet European Monetary Union (EMU) criteria in 1996, a year ahead of schedule. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell oil group considers selling a big part of its chemicals business. (p2)
- Unions reject KLM's planned restructuring measures. (p2) DE TELEGRAAF
- Microsoft chief Bill Gates gets honorary degree from Nijenrode University. (p3)
- Dutch businesses want cabinet to take steps to boost Europe's competitiveness during Dutch tenure of European Union's rotating presidency next year. (p25)
- Dutch transport firms are prepared to pay extra for motorway lanes reserved for trucks. (p27)
- Packaging concern Van Leer to build steel drum plant in Japan. (p27)
- Tank storage and transport concern Van Ommeren takes 40 pct stake in Norwegian tanker fleet operator Ivor Ships. (p27) TROUW
- PTT Telecom sees business opportunities in Brazil as country opens its mobile phones market. (p6) ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Environmental activists threaten to hold protests against companies using genetically modified soya beans. (p5)
- Decision on takeover of Fokker by Korea's Samsung expected soon. (p11)
